Bandits have abducted six people and rustled an unspecified number of goats and sheep during an attack on Dukkuma community in Sabon Birni Local Government Area of Sokoto State. PUNCH Metro learnt that the attack reportedly occurred on Tuesday night, leaving residents worried about the safety of their loved ones and the growing insecurity in rural communities across the state. However, the Sokoto State Police Command confirmed that six people were abducted during the incident, dismissing an earlier report that 14 residents were kidnapped. The state Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Ahmed Rufai, disclosed this in a text message to our correspondent on Thursday morning. He said, “Six people were abducted, while an unspecified number of goats and sheep were rustled.” DHQ denies supplying camouflage uniforms to suspected bandits Police arrest nine over armed robbery, rescues kidnapped victims in Nasarawa Bandits abduct six, rustle livestock in Sokoto The latest attack adds to the security concerns confronting residents of Sabon Birni and other communities in eastern Sokoto, which have repeatedly experienced bandit attacks, kidnappings and livestock rustling. This comes after armed bandits invaded the Yartsakuwa community in Rabah Local Government Area in the early hours of Sunday, November 15. The police spokesperson, Ahmed Rufai, confirmed that at least three people were killed, an unspecified number of residents were abducted, and livestock were rustled. A local survivor alleged that the death toll was four and noted that multiple women were taken from his family home. Both incidents have renewed concerns over the protection of rural communities and the need to strengthen security operations to prevent further attacks. Animashaun Salman
